course.title: Mathematics · Class 6
course.subject: mathematics
course.summary: Large numbers, estimation and fractions, built step by step with everyday examples.

skills.name: Read and write large numbers using place value
Understand a fraction as equal parts of a whole

sections.heading: Every digit has a place
sections.text: In 5,347 the digit 5 is in the **thousands** place, so it stands for 5,000. The same digit means a different amount depending on its place: this is **place value**.

sections.heading: Indian and international systems
sections.text: In the Indian system we group as thousands, lakhs and crores: 1,00,00,000 is one crore. In the international system we group in threes: 10,000,000 is ten million. Both write the same number.

sections.heading: Try it
sections.text: Write 7,25,48,316 in words using the Indian system. Then rewrite it with international commas.

questions.stem: What is the place value of 6 in 4,62,315?
questions.explanation: 6 is in the ten-thousands place, so it stands for 60,000.
hints: Count places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands…
The 6 is the fifth digit from the right.

misconceptions.0: That is the face value of the digit, not its place value.

questions.stem: How many lakhs make one crore?
hints: Write 1 lakh and 1 crore with all their zeros.

misconceptions.0: 10 lakhs is ten lakh = 10,00,000, which is one million.

questions.stem: Which is 3,05,020 written in words (Indian system)?
options: Three lakh fifty thousand two hundred
questions.explanation: 3 lakhs, 05 thousands, 0 hundreds, 20: three lakh five thousand twenty.

questions.stem: Ten million in the international system equals how much in the Indian system?
hints: Count the zeros: ten million has seven.

sections.heading: Comparing
sections.text: The number with **more digits** is bigger. If they have the same number of digits, compare from the left: the first place where the digits differ decides.

sections.heading: Rounding
sections.text: To round 4,68,512 to the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit (5). Five or more rounds up, so it becomes 4,69,000.

sections.heading: Estimating
sections.text: Estimation gives a quick, sensible answer. 5,290 + 17,986 is about 5,000 + 18,000 = 23,000 when rounded to the nearest thousand.

questions.explanation: The six-digit numbers are bigger; comparing them, 1,02,345 > 1,00,999.
The tens digit is 4 (less than 5), so round down to 7,800.

misconceptions.2: Only round up when the tens digit is 5 or more.

sections.heading: Equal parts
sections.text: A fraction names **equal parts** of a whole. If a roti is cut into 4 equal pieces and you eat 3, you ate 3/4 of it.

sections.heading: Numerator and denominator
sections.text: In 3/4 the **denominator** 4 says how many equal parts the whole has; the **numerator** 3 says how many parts we take.

sections.heading: Proper and improper
sections.text: In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller (2/5). In an improper fraction it is equal or bigger (7/4), which is more than one whole: 7/4 = 1 3/4.

questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices and 3 are eaten. What fraction is eaten?
questions.explanation: 3 parts taken out of 8 equal parts: 3/8.
hints: The denominator is the total number of equal parts.

misconceptions.1: 5/8 is the part left, not eaten.

questions.stem: In the fraction 5/9, what is the denominator?
questions.explanation: The denominator is the number below the line.
9 > 4, so 9/4 is improper (more than one whole).
hints: Compare the top and bottom numbers.

sections.heading: Same amount, different names
sections.text: 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 all describe the same amount. Fractions like these are **equivalent**.

sections.heading: Making equivalent fractions
sections.text: Multiply or divide the numerator **and** the denominator by the same non-zero number: 2/3 = (2×4)/(3×4) = 8/12.

sections.heading: Simplest form
sections.text: A fraction is in its simplest form when the numerator and denominator have no common factor except 1. 12/18 → divide both by 6 → 2/3.

hints: Do the same thing to top and bottom.

questions.explanation: Divide both by 8 (their greatest common factor): 2/3.
hints: Find the largest number that divides both.
